Backpropagation

In simple words

The method a neural network uses to work out how much each weight was to blame for a mistake.

The method that tells a neural network how to improve. After a wrong answer, it goes backwards through the network, layer by layer, and works out how much each weight added to the mistake. Gradient descent then nudges every weight a little.

Example. After a lost football match, a coach replays the video backwards from the goal you let in: who lost the ball, who was out of position? Then each player fixes their own part a little.

Related words

  • Neural networkAn AI model made of many simple connected units (neurons), arranged in layers, that learn patterns together.
  • Gradient descentA way to train a model by changing its parameters, step by step, in the direction that makes the loss smaller.
  • Loss functionA score that measures how wrong a model's answers are; training tries to make it as small as possible.
  • Parameters (weights)The numbers inside a model that change during training and store what it has learned.
